summary: @servicetitan/anvil-fonts preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package declares `scripts.preinstall: node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs is variable-obfuscated and, when a local `bun` binary is not found, downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/ into an OS temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it (`execFileSync`) against a sibling `math_init.js` shipped at the tarball root. `math_init.js` is a 727 KB single-line `@bun-cjs` bundle protected by a rotating string-array cipher (`n7gIxM` array, `WV8StW` rotator, `hc1jfK9` custom-base decoder) with hex-mangled identifiers — the payload is not inspectable as source. The package's declared purpose is font assets and its `dist/` tree already contains the CSS/font content the README advertises; downloading a second runtime to execute an opaque bundle is unrelated to that purpose. `package.json` declares `"files": ["dist", "readme.md"]`, so neither `setup.mjs` nor `math_init.js` is disclosed in the manifest, though both ship at the tarball root and are executed at install time. This is the alternate-runtime-dropper shape: the payload runs under a freshly-fetched non-Node runtime so Node-based review does not observe the executed code, granting arbitrary code execution on the installer's host during `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
